key_insight: This paper introduces a real-world, large-scale dataset to support automated evaluation of central line dressing change skills. It addresses a major bottleneck in healthcare training by enabling more scalable, consistent, and fine-grained assessment.
problem_solved: Traditional competency assessment for central line dressing change depends on manual observation by clinical educators, which is time-consuming, hard to scale, and often inconsistent across evaluators.
method: Collected a large-scale, real-world dataset focused on central line dressing change procedural performance.
Designed the dataset to support automated skill evaluation, enabling AI models to assess clinical procedure quality.
Aimed to capture data that can improve consistency, granularity, and scalability in competency assessment.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work provides a valuable benchmark dataset for developing and testing automated procedural skill assessment systems. It also opens the door to more scalable healthcare training tools that can reduce educator workload and improve patient safety.
visual_elements: Workflow diagram showing the central line dressing change procedure and where evaluation occurs
Dataset overview chart highlighting scale, participants, and data types
Comparison graphic of manual evaluation versus automated evaluation

paper_title: The Collection of a Real-World, Large-Scale Dataset for Automated Skill Evaluation in Central Line Dressing Change
paper_authors: Ummey Tanin, Shannan K. Hamlin, Hsin-Mei Chen,  Peizhu,  Qian
